subject.title: WhatsApp inbound messages not received in k3s nested container (outbound works)

question: Should WhatsApp external-inbound loss be solved with active liveness probing, provider-side reconnect backfill, explicit unrecoverable-gap diagnostics, or a combined recovery policy?
rationale: Current main only covers Baileys-delivered append catch-up; the remaining symptom spans transport liveness, provider history semantics, privacy/read-receipt behavior, and live WhatsApp proof that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Combined Recovery Design
options.body: Design a WhatsApp-plugin policy with active post-reconnect liveness, bounded monitored-chat backfill where reliable, and explicit warnings when messages cannot be recovered.

options.title: Warn-Only Diagnostics First
options.body: Add status and log diagnostics for inbound-stream gaps without attempting history replay until WhatsApp/Baileys backfill behavior is proven live.

options.title: Keep Append-Only Scope
options.body: Declare the bounded append catch-up behavior sufficient and close broader inbound-loss work only after maintainers explicitly accept the remaining container and zombie cases as out of scope.

recommendation.title: Combined Recovery Design
recommendation.body: Design a WhatsApp-plugin policy with active post-reconnect liveness, bounded monitored-chat backfill where reliable, and explicit warnings when messages cannot be recovered.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged the bounded reconnect catch-up and already documented the provider-side gap that this decision must resolve.
